_meta.title: The Baseline Register — every figure a financed-emissions disclosure rests on, linked to the asset classes that read it
_meta.purpose: The machine-readable half of the register: one entry per baseline, the PCAF asset classes and options that read it, every candidate value with its provenance and verification level, the value proposed for release, and the improvement step. Part 2 seeds the governed registry (src/domains/baseline) from the adopted candidates; tests/baseline-register.test.js holds this file and the document to one another.
_meta.rule: Where a published standard sets the figure, the standard's value wins and this holds only the citation; where none does, the figure is regional judgement and lives in the governed registry — scoped global → country → organisation, released, versioned, superseded only with a reason.
_meta.hierarchy: Sri Lankan published source → regional → global, the tier printed beside the figure wherever it is used; within a tier, verified reported → reported → physical activity → economic activity.

verificationLevels.primary: The publishing document was opened and the number read from it, with page or table cited. A disclosure may rest on it.
verificationLevels.secondary_reported: The figure and its citation come from a description of the primary source (a search excerpt, a third-party summary, a republisher); the document was not opened. A disclosure may not rest on it until re-read from the source — it is a worklist row with a URL.
verificationLevels.not_found: The source is known to exist but no figure could be evidenced. Reported absent with what is needed.

_meta.sessionConstraint: Compiled from a cloud session whose network policy refuses every general website; only GitHub raw content, Google Cloud Storage and one Amazon S3 bucket were reachable, so every Sri Lankan government, IEA, UNFCCC, CEB, SLSEA, DCS and vendor figure is secondary_reported. PCAF documents held in the repository and open datasets on those hosts are primary.
_meta.classification: Every product classifies by the substance of the financed asset into PCAF's asset classes — a home-purchase facility is a mortgage, a vehicle facility a motor vehicle loan, a facility to a business a business loan, a bond or sukuk holding a corporate bond or sovereign debt — exactly as for any bank. PCAF's classes are the only vocabulary; no instrument-specific layer sits on top.
